verdicts.claim: ARView (RealityKit, UIKit view) is NOT deprecated on the iOS 26 SDK (platforms: iOS 13.0, no deprecatedAt). It supports .ar and .nonAR camera modes, 2D->3D helpers and a collision hit test that returns per-triangle info on iOS 18.
verdicts.correction: The claim stands, including the part the verifier disputed. ARView: `@MainActor @objc @preconcurrency class ARView`, iOS 13.0, deprecated=false, no deprecatedAt (tvOS 26.0 newly added on the iOS 26 SDK). init(frame:cameraMode:) IS deprecated: its doc JSON platform entries for iOS 13.0, iPadOS 13.0 and Mac Catalyst 14.0 carry deprecated=true with renamed="init(frame:cameraMode:automaticallyConfigureSession:)" and no deprecatedAt version (an unversioned @available deprecation), so the researcher was right and the verifier's "deprecatedAt null so not deprecated" reading is rejected. Use `init(frame frameRect: CGRect, cameraMode: ARView.CameraMode, automaticallyConfigureSession: Bool)` (iOS 13.0, not deprecated), e.g. ARView(frame: .zero, cameraMode: .nonAR, automaticallyConfigureSession: false); calling the 2-arg init compiles with a deprecation warning only. Per-triangle hits: `var triangleHit: CollisionCastHit.TriangleHit? { get }` is iOS 18.0. I do accept the verifier's separate point (it concerns the NOTES rationale, not this claim text): RealityView on iOS 18 is NOT missing projection/hit-test helpers (RealityViewCameraContent conforms to RealityCoordinateSpaceProjecting, iOS 18.0). What ARView uniquely gives on iOS is ARSession access, raycast(from:allowing:alignment:) against ARKit geometry, debugOptions, snapshot(saveToHDR:completion:), installGestures(_:for:) and UIKit touch handling.
verdicts.reasoning: Ruling on the reality verdict: re-fetched arview.json (deprecated=false on all platforms), arview/init(frame:cameramode:).json (metadata.platforms[].deprecated=true, renamed to the 3-arg init, deprecatedAt absent) and arview/init(frame:cameramode:automaticallyconfiguresession:).json (deprecated=false). The verifier looked only at deprecatedAt/deprecationSummary, but DocC encodes an unversioned deprecation as deprecated=true without deprecatedAt, and the ARView page's references also mark init(frame:cameraMode:) deprecated=true. So verifier sub-point (1) is wrong. Sub-point (2) is correct but targets the notes, not the claim sentence, which is fully accurate. Hence the claim as written is not refuted.

verdicts.claim: RealityView (SwiftUI) exists on iOS 18.0 with a virtual camera and built-in gesture camera controls, but only ONE control mode at a time and no projection/raycast helpers on iOS.
verdicts.correction: Uphold the verifiers. RealityView (iOS 18.0) with content.camera = .virtual and .realityViewCameraControls(_:) is correct, and CameraControls (iOS 18.0, macOS 15.0, visionOS 2.0) is a struct with static members none, orbit, pan, tilt, dolly conforming only to Equatable/Hashable/Sendable/SendableMetatype (not an OptionSet), so only one control mode at a time. But "no projection/raycast helpers on iOS" is false: `struct RealityViewCameraContent` (iOS 18.0) conforms to `protocol RealityCoordinateSpaceProjecting` (iOS 18.0, macOS 15.0, tvOS 26.0, not visionOS), which provides `func project(point: SIMD3<Float>, to space: some CoordinateSpaceProtocol) -> CGPoint?`, `func unproject(_ point: CGPoint, from space: some CoordinateSpaceProtocol, to realitySpace: some RealityCoordinateSpace, ontoPlane planeTransform: float4x4) -> SIMD3<Float>?`, `func ray(through point: CGPoint, in space: some CoordinateSpaceProtocol, to realitySpace: some RealityCoordinateSpace) -> (origin: SIMD3<Float>, direction: SIMD3<Float>)?`, `func hitTest(point: CGPoint, in space: some CoordinateSpaceProtocol, query: CollisionCastQueryType, mask: CollisionGroup) -> [CollisionCastHit]`, `func entity(at point: CGPoint, in space: some CoordinateSpaceProtocol) -> Entity?` and entities(at:in:). Hit tests only see entities with a CollisionComponent. Also available on iOS 18: `Scene.pixelCast(from: SIMD3<Float>, to: SIMD3<Float>) async throws -> PixelCastHit?` which hits ModelComponent geometry without collision shapes. Still missing on iOS: attachments (init(make:update:attachments:) is visionOS 1.0 only) and RealityCoordinateSpaceConverting (visionOS only). Note the helpers are reached from the `content` value captured in make/update, so SwiftUI gesture code must hold onto it (or use EntityTargetValue in entity-targeted gestures).
verdicts.reasoning: Ruling on the official-docs verdict: re-fetched realityviewcameracontent.json (relationshipsSections Conforms To lists RealityCoordinateSpaceProjecting and RealityViewContentProtocol) and realitycoordinatespaceprojecting.json plus its project(point:to:), unproject(_:from:to:ontoplane:), ray(through:in:to:), hittest(point:in:query:mask:) and entity(at:in:) pages, all iOS 18.0 with deprecated=false. cameracontrols.json confirms single-mode struct. The researcher's statement is contradicted by primary docs; the verifier's correction is accurate and I found nothing to reject.

verdicts.claim: No built-in RealityKit material on iOS reads per-vertex colors (MeshDescriptor/MeshBuffers has no color semantic; UnlitMaterial/PBR ignore the LowLevelMesh .color attribute; ShaderGraphMaterial is visionOS-only). Vertex-color display therefore needs CustomMaterial with a Metal surface shader that reads params.geometry().color(). Per-FACE colors (classification, coverage) do NOT need shaders: use one material per color and per-face material indices (MeshDescriptor.materials = .perFace([UInt32]) or LowLevelMesh parts with materialIndex).
verdicts.correction: Uphold the verifiers on the load-bearing error. `struct ShaderGraphMaterial` is iOS 18.0, iPadOS 18.0, Mac Catalyst 18.0, macOS 15.0, tvOS 26.0, visionOS 1.0 (deprecated=false), and `init(materialXLabel: String, data: Data) async throws` has the same availability, so a MaterialX document embedded as a string (geomcolor node into a RealityKit unlit surface) can be loaded at runtime on iOS 18 without Reality Composer Pro or a .metal file. The Shader Graph Geometry Color node is iOS 17.0+. Therefore "Vertex-color display therefore needs CustomMaterial" is false: there are two paths on iOS 18, (a) `CustomMaterial` (iOS 15.0, no visionOS) with `init(surfaceShader: CustomMaterial.SurfaceShader, geometryModifier: CustomMaterial.GeometryModifier? = nil, lightingModel: CustomMaterial.LightingModel) throws` (lightingModel has no default) and a surface shader reading params.geometry().color() and writing set_emissive_color (under .unlit) or set_base_color (under .lit), and (b) ShaderGraphMaterial from MaterialX. The rest of the claim stands: MeshBuffers/MeshDescriptor have no color semantic, UnlitMaterial/PhysicallyBasedMaterial ignore LowLevelMesh .color (Apple engineer, forum 759449), and per-face colors via one material per color with MeshDescriptor.Materials .perFace([UInt32]) (iOS 15.0) or LowLevelMesh.Part materialIndex (iOS 18.0) need no shaders. Recommended architecture: use per-face material indices for classification/coverage; for true per-vertex color, try ShaderGraphMaterial(materialXLabel:data:) first (no Metal toolchain dependency in CI) and keep CustomMaterial as fallback; verify both render LowLevelMesh .color on device in an early build.
verdicts.reasoning: Ruling on the official-docs verdict: re-fetched shadergraphmaterial.json and shadergraphmaterial/init(materialxlabel:data:).json (iOS 18.0, deprecated=false), shadergraph/geometric/geometry-color.json (iOS 17.0) and custommaterial.json (iOS 15.0, no visionOS). The claim's "ShaderGraphMaterial is visionOS-only" reflects 2023 (visionOS 1 era) documentation and is out of date since the iOS 18 SDK. The verifier's correction is accurate; I reject nothing of it except to stress that iOS rendering of LowLevelMesh .color through either path still lacks a compiled iOS sample.

open_question_answers.question: Does params.geometry().color() in a CustomMaterial surface shader return the LowLevelMesh .color (uchar4Normalized_bgra) attribute on iOS 18? Strongly implied (VertexSemantic.color exists for this; visionOS shader-graph 'Geometry Color' reads it) but no compiled iOS sample was found. Verify in the first build; fallback: pack colour into uv1/uv0 or use per-face material parts.
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test: render a LowLevelMesh with a .color attribute (uchar4Normalized_bgra) using a CustomMaterial whose surface shader writes params.geometry().color().rgb to emissive under .unlit, and log/screenshot whether colors or white appear; do the same with ShaderGraphMaterial(materialXLabel:data:) (geomcolor to unlit surface). Best evidence: Metal-RealityKit-APIs.pdf documents surface::geometry::color() as the fragment's interpolated vertex color, and an Apple engineer (forum 759449) says all LowLevelMesh vertex attributes including color are exposed to Shader Graph; no compiled iOS sample found. Keep the per-face material fallback.

open_question_answers.question: Measured RealityKit frame rate on iPhone 13 Pro Max with ~1M triangles in ~200-400 LowLevelMesh entities using CustomMaterial vs UnlitMaterial: no public benchmark exists; needs an on-device test (Apple: 'measure and iterate').
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test: on iPhone 13 Pro Max, load a ~1M triangle scan split into 200-400 LowLevelMesh entities, log frame time (CADisplayLink or ARView/RealityView frame updates via SceneEvents.Update deltas) and thermal state for UnlitMaterial vs CustomMaterial vs ShaderGraphMaterial. No public benchmark exists; design the viewer so the material type is swappable and chunk count is tunable.

open_question_answers.question: Exact triangleHit.faceIndex semantics when a CollisionComponent holds several ShapeResources (index relative to shapeIndex) and whether faceIndex matches the source triangle order of generateStaticMesh(from: MeshResource) (expected yes; verify by picking a known triangle).
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test: build a CollisionComponent from ShapeResource.generateStaticMesh(from:) for a mesh with known triangle order, hit known triangles and log triangleHit.faceIndex (iOS 18.0) and shapeIndex. Docs do not define the multi-shape mapping; architecture should use one static-mesh shape per chunk entity so faceIndex only needs to be mapped within one shape, and keep a CPU-side ray-triangle fallback for measurement snapping.

open_question_answers.question: pixelCast(from:to:) cost and whether primitive indexes triangles in original index order for a LowLevelMesh with multiple parts (meshPart id mapping is undocumented).
open_question_answers.answer: Partly answered: the API is `Scene.pixelCast(from startPosition: SIMD3<Float>, to endPosition: SIMD3<Float>) async throws -> PixelCastHit?` (iOS 18.0, macOS 15.0; not listed for visionOS), it ray casts against rendered geometry and ignores entities without a ModelComponent with a valid mesh, so no CollisionComponent is needed. Because it is async and GPU-backed, treat it as a per-tap query, not a per-frame one. Cost and primitive-index-to-part mapping: needs device test (log latency per call and compare returned primitive index against known triangles in a multi-part LowLevelMesh).

open_question_answers.question: Whether MeshResource.generate(from: [MeshDescriptor]) is still present in the iOS 26 SDK headers (the doc JSON only lists the Contents overload; community code uses the descriptor overload everywhere). Only matters if you use MeshDescriptor instead of LowLevelMesh.
open_question_answers.answer: Likely present. The MeshResource doc JSON only has pages for generate(from: MeshResource.Contents), but meshdescriptor.json's own discussion links `MeshResource/generate(from:)-6l1q2`, a disambiguated symbol distinct from the Contents overload (-4aahn), whose page returns 404; that indicates a second, undocumented-but-existing overload rather than a removal. Nothing marks it deprecated. The architecture should prefer LowLevelMesh plus `MeshResource(from: LowLevelMesh) async throws` (iOS 18.0) for scan meshes anyway; if MeshDescriptor is used, confirm with one CI compile.

open_question_answers.question: Whether iOS 26's reworked RealityKit renderer changes CustomMaterial or triangleFillMode behaviour on the second (iOS 26) phone; nothing in the docs indicates deprecation of either.
open_question_answers.answer: needs device test on the iOS 26 phone: run the same CustomMaterial, ShaderGraphMaterial and debug wireframe (triangleFillMode) scenes and compare screenshots and logs. On the iOS 26 SDK docs, CustomMaterial (iOS 15.0) and ShaderGraphMaterial are not deprecated and gained tvOS 26.0 entries, so no API removal is indicated.

open_question_answers.question: RealityView on iOS: whether Apple will add combined camera controls or project/unproject; until then ARView remains the practical host, and there is no Apple statement deprecating ARView (forum 788284 has no Apple reply).
open_question_answers.answer: Premise partly wrong: RealityView on iOS 18 already has project/unproject/ray/hitTest via RealityViewCameraContent conforming to RealityCoordinateSpaceProjecting (iOS 18.0). CameraControls on the iOS 26 SDK still has single modes only (none, orbit, pan, tilt, dolly; not an OptionSet), so combined orbit plus pan plus pinch needs custom gestures either way. ARView is not deprecated on the iOS 26 SDK (only its 2-arg init(frame:cameraMode:) is). Recommendation: ARView(frame:cameraMode: .nonAR, automaticallyConfigureSession: false) in a UIViewRepresentable with a PerspectiveCamera driven by custom UIKit gestures remains the lowest-risk viewer host on iOS 18 (snapshot, debugOptions, full touch control), and the same ARView in .ar mode serves scanning; RealityView is a viable alternative host if SwiftUI-native is preferred.
